verdict.rationale: The Angular CLI documents a first-party command that "builds and serves an Angular application, then runs end-to-end tests". That is the product's own e2e integration tied to its dev server. However, the evidence never names the official e2e framework or shows it working without extra setup. The only tool reference is a dated community mention of Protractor in the AngularJS era. Missing for 10: identification of an official e2e test runner, evidence that it works out of the box without added packages or configuration, in-depth docs on the e2e workflow, and independent hands-on corroboration for modern Angular.
